title.narrative: Clean Drinking Water and Hygiene with a Gender focus

description.narrative:
The project aims to bring the following outcome:
More women and men in arid land communities of Kitui, Maralal and Marsabi influence the policies and practices that improve sustainable access, control, management and safe use of water resources assets and access to clean water and practice safe environmental sanitation and hygiene benefiting 22,550 individuals.
CAFOD Partners, The Catholic diocese of Kitui, Isiolo, Marsabit and Mararal have in the past initiated a number of projects funded by CAFOD and other partners. A big portion of the projects have gone into provision of water for human and livestock consumption. Most of the water facilities are provided through boreholes, water pans and rock catchments. Whereas rock catchments and boreholes may provide clean drinking water if hygienically maintained, the earth dams provided have no facilities to provide clean drinking water for human consumption. Some of the boreholes provided are of high salinity especially in Kargi, Marsabit and there is speculation that they contain heavy metals that can cause diseases. Most of the project beneficiaries are pastoralists. The coverage of latrines is very low in the community and due to open defecation; there is likelihood of contamination of the water sources. Due to low levels of education in the community, hygiene awareness is very low. The project aims at increasing accessibility of sufficient potable water to the community while at the same time addressing the need for safe defecation through Community Led total Sanitation programme which aims at sensitizing the community to construct their own latrines with no material support. The project also aims at sensitizing the community in safe hygiene through simple messages on safe water (drinking only from safe water source or home treatment), safe defecation and hand washing at critical times. The project further aims at carrying out a gender analysis and sensitizing the community leaders on gender roles and women participation with the aim of having active women leadership in the committees. The project therefore aims to address the following mach fund outcome indicators:
-number of men and women reporting access to safe drinking water, -number of women and men reporting access to sanitation facilities, -number of women and men of targeted beneficiaries demonstrating good hygiene practice, -number of women engaged in WASH and environmental management committees reporting increased opportunity and confidence in decisions affecting access to and safe use of household and/or community resources such as water -CAFOD partners showing evidence of gender analysis throughout the project cycle and using sex disaggregated data in monitoring and reporting.
